requirement:
# REQ-2283: Generator and analyzer crash with IndexOutOfRangeException on a closed generic struct from a referenced assembly

Source: https://github.com/MessagePack-CSharp/MessagePack-CSharp/issues/2283

#### Bug description

Both `MessagePackGenerator` (CS8785) and `MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer` (AD0001) throw `IndexOutOfRangeException` when a `[MessagePackObject]` type has a member whose type is a **closed generic value type defined in a referenced assembly**.

Because the generator then "will not contribute to the output", the compiling assembly silently ends up with **no generated resolver at all**. It is only a warning, so a normal build looks fine, but trimmed and NativeAOT apps fail at runtime. In our case three assemblies of a large app had been shipping without a resolver across two releases before we noticed.

#### Repro steps

Two projects. `lib`:

```csharp
using MessagePack;
namespace Lib;

[MessagePackObject]
public partial record struct Item<T>([property: Key(0)] string Key);
```

`app`, with a `ProjectReference` to `lib`:

```csharp
using MessagePack; using Lib;
namespace App;

[MessagePackObject]
public sealed partial record Cmd([property: Key(0)] string Scope)
{
    [Key(1)] public Item<int> Member { get; init; }
}
```

Then `dotnet build` on `app`. Both projects are in the attached `mp-repro.zip`.

#### Expected behavior

A clean build, with a generated resolver in `app`.
#### Actual behavior

```
CSC : warning CS8785: Generator 'MessagePackGenerator' failed to generate source. It will not
contribute to the output and compilation errors may occur as a result. Exception was of type
'IndexOutOfRangeException' with message 'Index was outside the bounds of the array.'.
CSC : warning AD0001: Analyzer 'MessagePack.SourceGenerator.Analyzers.MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer'
threw an exception of type 'System.IndexOutOfRangeException' with message 'Index was outside the
bounds of the array.'.
```

`app.dll` contains no `GeneratedMessagePackResolver`.

- Version used: MessagePack 3.1.8
- Runtime: .NET 10 (SDK 10.0.204), Windows 11

#### Additional context

**What triggers it.** `Item` is declared in `lib`, `Cmd` in `app`:

| `Item` declared as | result |
|---|---|
| `record struct Item<T>` | **crash** |
| `struct Item<T>` | **crash** |
| `struct Item` | ok |
| `record struct Item` | ok |
| `class Item<T>` | ok |
| `record class Item<T>` | ok |

So it needs all three of: **generic**, **value type**, **from a referenced assembly**. Moving the identical `Item<T>` declaration into `app` itself makes the crash disappear, which is what makes this specific to metadata symbols.
**Stack trace.**

```
System.IndexOutOfRangeException: Index was outside the bounds of the array.
   at TypeCollector.GetObjectInfo(INamedTypeSymbol formattedType, ISymbol callerSymbol)
   at TypeCollector.CollectGeneric(INamedTypeSymbol type, ISymbol callerSymbol) in TypeCollector.cs:line 661
   at TypeCollector.CollectCore(ITypeSymbol typeSymbol, ISymbol callerSymbol) in TypeCollector.cs:line 371
   at TypeCollector.GetObjectInfo(INamedTypeSymbol formattedType, ISymbol callerSymbol) in TypeCollector.cs:line 1062
   at TypeCollector.CollectCore(ITypeSymbol typeSymbol, ISymbol callerSymbol) in TypeCollector.cs:line 386
   at TypeCollector.Collect() in TypeCollector.cs:line 300
   at MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer.AnalyzeSymbol(SymbolAnalysisContext, ReferenceSymbols, AnalyzerOptions) in MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer.cs:line 431
```

`CollectGeneric` line 661 is the closed-generic branch that calls `GetObjectInfo` directly:

```csharp
else
{
    // NOTE: ... closed generic types such as `Foo<string>` are not registered as a formatter.
    this.GetObjectInfo(type, callerSymbol);
```

so `GetObjectInfo` runs against a type that has no syntax. Several diagnostic paths inside it index `DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0]` directly (lines 735, 1009, 1101) instead of using `FirstOrDefault()` the way the neighbouring `GetIdentifierLocation` / `GetLocation` / `GetParameterListLocation` helpers already do, and that collection is empty for a metadata symbol. I did not narrow down which of the three fires.

**Getting the stack trace.** Console output truncates the exception to its message; `-p:ErrorLog=out.sarif` preserves the full description, including the stack trace and an `ISymbol:` context line naming the offending type:

```
dotnet build -p:ErrorLog=out.sarif
```

**Workaround.** Putting `[MessagePackFormatter(typeof(ItemFormatter<>))]` on the generic value type short-circuits `CollectCore` (line 356) before `GetObjectInfo` is reached, at the cost of hand-writing the formatter.

**Possibly related:** #2092 reports CS8785 from the v3 generator, but with a different inner exception and no repro.

story.summary: Stops the generator and the MsgPack00x analyzer from crashing on a closed generic struct from a referenced assembly. It does three things. Two diagnostic sites in TypeCollector.GetObjectInfo no longer index `DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0]`. Every analyzer diagnostic now goes through a filter that drops any diagnostic not located in a source tree of the current compilation. Three tests compile a defining assembly to metadata and check that the consuming project builds with no warnings and gets a generated resolver. The change also adds two doc sections and an unrelated change to MessagePackSecurity.GetEqualityComparer.
story.why: For metadata symbols, `DeclaringSyntaxReferences` is empty, so `[0]` threw IndexOutOfRangeException. The generator then produced no resolver at all.
touches_beyond_requirement: src/MessagePack/MessagePackSecurity.cs: GetEqualityComparer<string> now always returns EqualityComparer<string>.Default, even when HashCollisionResistant is on. This is a runtime security change unrelated to the issue.

TypeCollector line 239: a global diagnostic filter. It drops every analyzer diagnostic whose location is not in source, including Location.None diagnostics about types declared in source, not only metadata ones.
README.md and doc/analyzers/MsgPack004.md: new documentation sections.
story.confidence_overview: Medium-high that the reported repro no longer crashes. The record-struct test copies the issue's repro, and the test helper checks both for no warnings and for the resolver hint name. The issue lists three crash sites, but the diff changes only two, and no test shows the third is unreachable. The diagnostic filter is broader than needed. The MessagePackSecurity edit is out of scope and weakens hash-collision protection on platforms without randomized string hashing.

claims.text: The BothStringAndIntKeyAreNull diagnostic now gets its location from GetPropertyIdentifierLocation. That helper uses FirstOrDefault plus an `as PropertyDeclarationSyntax` cast and returns null instead of throwing when the property has no source syntax.
claims.requirement_quote: Several diagnostic paths inside it index `DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0]` directly

claims.text: The README gains a section saying closed generic types from referenced assemblies are supported, and that diagnostics about their members are reported only by the defining assembly.
MsgPack004.md gains a section saying the analyzer reports only on members declared in the current project.
Scope: the MessagePackSecurity.GetEqualityComparer change, which short-circuits for string, serves no requirement text and has no test.

When the analyzer supplies a reporter, every diagnostic is passed through ReportIfLocatedInCompilation. That method forwards a diagnostic only if its Location.IsInSource is true and its SourceTree belongs to the current compilation; otherwise it drops it.

The MemberNeedsKey diagnostic is built with `DeclaringSyntaxReferences.FirstOrDefault()?.GetSyntax().GetLocation()`. That expression runs even when no reporter is set (for example in generator mode), so it no longer throws for an unkeyed member of a metadata type.
claims.requirement_quote: Several diagnostic paths inside it index `DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0]` directly

claims.text: Test ClosedGenericStruct_FromMetadataReference compiles a generic struct into a separate metadata-only assembly and uses `MyGenericStruct<int>` as a member. It then verifies there are no diagnostics and that the resolver is generated.
claims.requirement_quote: A clean build, with a generated resolver in `app`.

claims.text: Test ClosedGenericRecordStruct_FromMetadataReference reproduces the issue's `Item<T>`/`Cmd` sources verbatim, using the Latest language version. It asserts a clean run and that App.AppResolver.g.cs is generated.
claims.requirement_quote: A clean build, with a generated resolver in `app`.

claims.text: Test ClosedGenericStruct_FromMetadataReference_UnkeyedMember uses a metadata struct with a public unkeyed member. It asserts that no diagnostic is reported in the consuming project and that the resolver is still generated. This exercises the MemberNeedsKey path together with the location filter.
claims.requirement_quote: So it needs all three of: **generic**, **value type**, **from a referenced assembly**.

claims.text: RunWithMetadataReferenceAsync works in two steps. First it runs the verifier with the defining assembly added only as a metadata reference and fails on any diagnostic. Then it runs the generator driver directly, asserts there are no warning-or-higher diagnostics (CS8785 would be caught here), and asserts the expected resolver hint name is among the generated sources.

The test helpers CompileToMetadataReferenceAsync and CreateCompilation emit the defining source to an in-memory image against net8.0 plus the MessagePack references, and throw if emit fails. The new usings support these helpers.
claims.requirement_quote: Moving the identical `Item<T>` declaration into `app` itself makes the crash disappear, which is what makes this specific to metadata symbols.

refusals.what: GetEqualityComparer<string> bypasses the hash-collision-resistant comparer under UntrustedData.
refusals.why: This changes how untrusted deserialized input is hashed and weakens DoS protection on runtimes without randomized string hashing.

refusals.what: Unrelated runtime change bundled into a source-generator crash fix.
refusals.why: It goes beyond the requirement, and no test covers it.

refusals.what: A global analyzer diagnostic filter that suppresses all non-source-located diagnostics.
refusals.why: This is a user-visible policy change: diagnostics are silently dropped for source types as well. It goes further than replacing the `[0]` indexing that the requirement asks for.

findings.description: GetEqualityComparer<string> now returns EqualityComparer<string>.Default even when HashCollisionResistant (UntrustedData) is on. string.GetHashCode is not randomized on .NET Framework, which the netstandard2.0 build can run on. This reopens hash-flooding DoS for string-keyed dictionaries deserialized from untrusted data. Static check S6 did not catch it. It is unrelated to the issue.

The filter drops every diagnostic with Location.None, not only diagnostics about metadata types. A source-declared type whose location helper returns null now has its diagnostic silently suppressed. One example is a positional record property, where GetPropertyIdentifierLocation returns null because the syntax is a ParameterSyntax. Analyzers are allowed to report at Location.None, so the comment at 1440-1442 overstates the constraint.

Previously a hard cast to PropertyDeclarationSyntax; now `as`. For a positional record property in source, the location becomes null and the line 239 filter then drops the BothStringAndIntKeyAreNull diagnostic instead of reporting it.

The issue lists three `DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0]` sites (old lines 735, 1009, 1101), but the diff changes only two. Any remaining unguarded `[0]` index in GetObjectInfo or its helpers has not been verified or fixed, and other metadata shapes could still crash.

The docs say problems are reported by the defining assembly. If that assembly was not built with the MessagePack analyzer (for example, a third-party NuGet package), unkeyed members are silently ignored in the consumer, with no diagnostic anywhere.
